prop: This design was built against the tetel repository at commit 67191f58c925fcaaed5f9b2ebe218bb23fcded8e ("tet28: pin the census refusal, and make the parity guard real"), with a clean working tree at the start of authoring; the TET-28 modification-target implementation is present in the tree this design reads, and the memo plus its snapshot are the one addition this workspace makes.

TET-29's trigger must be a declaration, not a detection, by the same argument TET-28 implemented rather than merely designed. "Any design or fix that transplants a mechanism from another site" denotes no enumerable set of records: nothing in the record model types a claim or prose block as a transplant, and deciding from English (or from comparing code across two sites) that a fix "transplants" is a heuristic read — the class scope.rs measured dead for symbol mentions ("naming a symbol the code you read calls is normal; concluding about it is the failure; the two are not distinguishable by string matching") and the class targets.rs's shipped doc comment rules out as a refusal trigger. So a transplant is a record the author declares, the refusal attaches to the declaration, and under-declaration is handled the way TET-28 handles it: an always-rendered section that shows its hole, plus a printed non-coverage line, never a detector.

"Transcribed verbatim" cannot be an honour-system field, and does not need to be: the decidable relation is that a premise's text is refused unless it is a verbatim substring of the cited donor fact's captured output. Both sides of that comparison are Strings the tool controls — a fact's output is produced only by look/run (file bytes read verbatim by look_path, grep match lines, a process's merged stream), no authoring surface lets anyone supply output by hand, and output is immutable after mint — so substring containment is a pure byte-level comparison with no normalisation step owned by the check. Typing is the selection mechanism, not the trust: the author types the premise, but a typed premise the donor never wrote fails containment and is refused at the verb. This is exactly the README's Direction item for supporting-span selection ("refused unless it is a verbatim substring of a cited fact — the author cannot type an extent, and here could not invent support, only select it"), and TET-29 is the first place it becomes load-bearing rather than roadmap.

The strictness objections to byte-level containment dissolve on the actual capture path, and every weaker relation reopens the invention channel. A donor comment wrapped across lines with interior prefix noise (`//`, `*`, indentation) IS a contiguous byte substring of a look_path capture, because look_path stores the file's bytes verbatim — the cost is only that the selected premise carries its comment syntax into the rendered section, which the "never paraphrase" constraint endorses rather than tolerates. Stripping that noise would require knowing each language's comment syntax, which is precisely the hard-coded per-language coupling scope.rs's "language-agnostic by construction" doctrine excludes. Two capture modes genuinely fight containment — grep-derived match outputs interleave "lineno:" prefixes between lines, and whole-search/no-match records carry empty output — so the design's guidance is that a donor fact is minted from `look` of the donor file; that is guidance about which observation to select from, not a new rule, since the relation is indifferent to which kind produced the bytes. Weaker relations fail: per-line containment lets an author stitch non-adjacent lines into a sentence the donor never wrote, and whitespace- or case-normalised matching means the memo shows text the capture does not contain — both are paraphrase with extra steps.

Containment against a fact's whole output has one genuine unsoundness, and it is fixable by the same schema move TET-28 already made. Fact.output is built at mint by joining the buffer entries' non-empty outputs with "\n", and the per-entry boundaries are not stored — so "substring of fact.output" can be satisfied by text straddling the seam between two observations: bytes that were never contiguous in anything the author actually saw, e.g. the tail of one file's capture concatenated with the head of another's. The fix is a serde-defaulted per-entry field on ExtentEntry recording the entry's output byte length, mirroring exactly how kind and pattern were added for TET-28: boundaries become reconstructible from lengths (skipping zero-length entries, matching the mint-time filter), the premise relation is then "verbatim substring of a single observation's output", and a donor fact minted before the field existed is ineligible with the same remedy TET-28 gives legacy facts — re-look and re-mint. Absent means not recorded, never guessed.

The transplant record's shape follows from precedents already shipped, one field at a time. A transplant is an append-only record declared by a new verb (one dispatch shared by CLI and MCP, one new Kind variant and counter): (a) the donor is a citation of exactly ONE fact — the same single-citation rationale targets.rs states ("a target resting on 'one of these several facts' would leave which one undecided"), and a fact citation rather than a typed path because the donor site is then the fact's captured extent, which no author can type; (b) premise rows are verbatim selections from that donor fact's output (per C3-C5), immutable once selected — a selection of immutable bytes has nothing to revise honestly — and withdrawable with --why, mirroring target's withdraw-not-revise discipline; (c) a premise is discharged by citing a claim, in a separate later act, and because `tetel claim` refuses without --cites and on unknown fact ids, a discharge claim rests on at least one real fact by construction — the ticket's "must that claim itself rest on a fact?" is answered yes with zero new machinery; (d) a discharge can be superseded by a later discharge citing a different claim, append-only, so a refuted-and-replaced claim does not strand its premise.

The transplant's destination should be a citation of a live modification target (T#), not a typed path and not an independent record — the two features compose. A transplant installs the donor's mechanism at a site the design necessarily tells the implementer to modify, so under TET-28's own rule that site should already be a declared target; making the transplant verb refuse a destination that is not a live target turns one declaration into a forcing function for the other, and narrows TET-28's admitted under-declaration blind spot for exactly the fix-shape that produced the motivating defect. The composition costs nothing at the edge cases: a green-field destination (new code, new symbol) is still censusable, because censuses() deliberately accepts a NoMatch search — "a symbol with no occurrences is censused by the grep that established it has none" — so declaring a target for a symbol that does not exist yet works today; and the destination-holds claims get a named, censused destination instead of a prose phrase. What the tool cannot verify — that the cited target really is where the mechanism lands — is content, and stays printed as non-coverage rather than guessed at.

An undischarged premise must be a legal workspace state, so the ticket's refusal cannot all move to the verb the way TET-28's did. The instrument works by transcribe-first: the author selects the donor's premises before knowing whether each holds at the destination — the confrontation the section exists to force. Refusing a premise row that cites no claim at declaration time would demand the destination-holds claim exist before the premise can be recorded, inverting that order (answer first, transcribe after) and pushing an author who cannot yet discharge a premise toward not declaring it at all — the same "refusing would make the honest case unwritable to catch the dishonest one" failure scope.rs's discriminator names. TET-28 never faced this because a census either exists or does not; a premise inventory is built across time. So the workspace invariant enforced at the verb is only "every premise is a genuine quotation of the cited donor's capture" (plus: donor fact exists and carries span boundaries, destination target exists and is live, a discharge cites an existing live claim); "every premise is discharged" is not a workspace invariant at all — it is a property of the finished document.

The refusals land on three surfaces, each the earliest that can decide its own question. (1) At the verb: quotation invariants — donor fact exists and is span-eligible, premise text is a verbatim substring of a single observation's output, destination is a live target, a discharge names an existing live claim. These are per-record and decidable at creation, exactly like target's census refusal. (2) At `render --out`: completeness — a live transplant with an undischarged premise (none cited, or its discharge claim withdrawn) refuses the write. This is deliberately later than the verb (the intermediate state is legal while authoring) and deliberately earlier than check (the ticket's placement): --out is the act that writes the reviewable artifact and its snapshot under the pinned policy that a rendered memo is never hand-edited, so a memo with a declared-but-unexamined premise should fail to come into existence rather than exist and fail; the remedy is singular — discharge the premise, or withdraw it or its transplant with --why. A preview render (no --out) still assembles, marking undischarged rows loudly, so mid-work visibility is preserved; this render/--out asymmetry is new, and it is the design's most debatable departure. (3) At check: re-verification of everything above against the shipped snapshot — both directions, since tampering can go either way (a transplant row the snapshot lacks; a snapshot premise whose text is not contained in its donor fact's output; a premise whose discharge claim is withdrawn or missing) — as a machine failure in the same partition as uncensused targets, with rows in a snapshotless document reported human-owed as unverifiable, the standing choice for snapshot-dependent findings. Containment is re-checked byte-for-byte from facts.jsonl, which already ships full outputs; check runs nothing and fetches nothing to do it.

The containment relation was tested against the motivating case itself, at the source, and it passes — with one correction to the ticket's framing. The missed premise ("its parent is remote-known or was walked earlier in this same session", remote_utils.rs:4576 in lonic-forklift at HEAD) is contiguous bytes in a raw capture of the donor file, both as a single clause within one line and as the full seven-line `//` comment with its prefixes, so the verbatim-substring refusal admits it without any comment-syntax knowledge. But the premise does NOT live in the donor function's `///` doc block — collect_changed_closure's doc block never states the insert-before-check discipline or its ordering premise; both live only in the body comment below the signature. So the ticket's phrase "the donor's comment-stated premises" must not be operationalised as "the donor's doc block": the relation has to range over whatever bytes the author captured of the donor site, and a premise stated at a call site or in a body comment is selectable exactly when the author's donor fact folded an observation that covers it — the relation thereby pressures the author to capture the donor widely enough, and a known-but-uncaptured premise demands another look, not a typed row. Separately, today's repaired destination twin states the once-missed condition as one gradeable sentence ("Sound only parents-first — a child that marked a parent-explained hash would otherwise short-circuit the explaining parent's own audit"), which is concrete evidence that the discharge obligation this design demands — one claim per premise, stating that it holds at the destination — fits in a single claim proposition for the hardest observed case.

The rendered section follows compose.rs's shipped conventions with one deliberate difference. A "## Transplants" section renders beside the modification-target section: per live transplant, the donor fact id with its extent labels (labels, never absolute keys — the committed-document rule), the destination target id and symbol, and one entry per live premise carrying the selected text verbatim in a fenced block with the discharging claim id beside it; withdrawn transplants and premises are dropped, and once any claim exists the section renders even when empty ("none declared"), because the hole is the finding — the same visibility answer to under-declaration the target section shipped. The deliberate difference: compose.rs refuses to inline captured output into the document because output is unbounded, but a premise is an author-bounded selection, not a whole capture, so inlining it verbatim is both safe and the entire point — the reader must see the donor's clause on the page, spelled the way the donor's file spells it, or the section is a list of opaque pointers. Fenced blocks rather than table cells because a premise legitimately spans lines and markdown table cells cannot carry multi-line verbatim text without escaping, which would violate byte-fidelity.

What the mechanism cannot catch is boundable and belongs in check's printed NON_COVERAGE list, which exists for exactly this ("a refusal that fired is easily read as coverage it never claimed"). Six entries: (a) a transplant the author never declared — no refusal can reach it; the empty section is its only trace; (b) premises the donor never wrote down — the relation selects from captured text, so a premise that lives in the donor's structure rather than its comments has nothing to select; (c) premises outside the captured extent — a donor fact that folded too narrow a look cannot yield a premise from the lines it never captured; (d) shallow selection — the tool verifies that selected bytes are the donor's, never that they are all the load-bearing ones; selecting one convenient clause and stopping is invisible to any format-level check, because deciding what counts as a premise is design judgment (the ticket says so) and deciding a selection is too small is a truth-check, the insincere-examination ceiling this project registered as permanently out of reach; (e) whether the discharge claim actually addresses its premise, and whether the cited target really is the mechanism's destination — both content; the claim is graded by a grounding pass as written, and the linkage is graded by nobody; (f) a donor comment that is itself wrong — verbatim quotation establishes provenance, never truth. None of these is reachable by a format-level refusal, so printing them is the honest disposition, not a fallback.

The mechanism's value is precisely that it moves one property across check's oldest declared blind spot, and grounding then does the rest. The FORK-94 defect's violated property was asserted by no claim at all — "dependents that never declared themselves", the first entry in the standing non-coverage list — which is why two correct grounding passes over the remedy could not see it: a grounder grades propositions as written, and there was no proposition. Every piece of this design funnels toward converting that absent proposition into a present one: the premise row forces the donor's condition onto the page as captured bytes, and the discharge obligation forces a claim that the condition holds at the destination — a claim like any other, resting on facts by construction, entering the evidence ledger, graded by the next grounding pass, revisable and then out-of-proof until regraded. The tool never judges whether the claim is true; it refuses only the shape in which the question goes unasked. The motivating case shows the converted claim would have been one sentence — and false, hence gradeable as false.

The implementation surface is small and every piece extends a mechanism already in the tree: one serde-defaulted per-entry output-length field on ExtentEntry (the same compatibility precedent that added kind and pattern, with the same absent-means-ineligible reading); one new record kind with its counter and id prefix; one transplants.jsonl appended by one CLI/MCP-shared dispatch, shipped by adding one line to snapshot.rs's deliberately-enumerated SNAPSHOT_FILES (whose targets.jsonl entry already documents why a record log must ship: without it the refusal "would hold only inside the workspace that authored the memo"); one rendered section beside render_targets; one completeness refusal in the render --out path; one check re-verifying from files the snapshot already carries (transplant machine findings beside uncensused_targets, unverifiable rows human-owed without a snapshot); and the new NON_COVERAGE lines. Nothing parses any programming language, nothing is re-run at check time, and no aggregate, score, or document-level verdict is introduced anywhere.

The mechanism's value is precisely that it moves one property across check's oldest declared blind spot, and grounding then does the rest. Per the ticket's account of the FORK-94 trail — recorded here as the ticket's report, not re-established — the defective remedy was graded supports twice, correctly, because the violated property was asserted by no claim at all; that situation is exactly the first entry in check's standing non-coverage list, "dependents that never declared themselves", and a grounder that grades propositions as written has nothing to grade where there is no proposition. Every piece of this design funnels toward converting that absent proposition into a present one: the premise row forces the donor's condition onto the page as captured bytes, and the discharge obligation forces a claim that the condition holds at the destination — a claim like any other, resting on facts by construction, entering the evidence ledger, graded by the next grounding pass, revisable and then out-of-proof until regraded. The tool never judges whether the claim is true; it refuses only the shape in which the question goes unasked. And the hardest observed case shows the converted claim fits in one sentence: today's repaired destination states the once-missed condition in a single doc-comment sentence, first-hand evidence that the discharge obligation is one gradeable proposition, not an essay.
why: The claim asserted FORK-94's grading history (two supports verdicts, the attack-pass chronology) as established fact, but that trail lives in the ticket, not in anything this workspace observed; the claim should carry it as the ticket's report, the same disposition TET-28's memo used for its private-trail premise. The in-repo halves (non-coverage entry, claim mechanics, the one-sentence destination condition) stay asserted first-hand.
